newsitem.title: USA: US OCC approves Waterhouse unit designation.
newsitem.headline: US OCC approves Waterhouse unit designation.

text.p: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency said Tuesday it will evaluate Waterhouse National Bank under "limited-purpose" institution criteria for compliance with the Community Reinvestment Act.
Waterhouse is a unit of Waterhouse Investor Services Inc. which has a pending merger with Toronto-Dominion Bank. The merger application is before the Federal Reserve.

Separately, Waterhouse's bank unit applied for the limited-purpose designation from the OCC and it was recently approved, an OCC spokesman confirmed. The designation sets the criteria with which the bank will be evaluated under the CRA.
The CRA aims to ensure banks serve poorer neighborhoods. Banks which offer traditional products such as mortgages and business loans are evaluated on where those loans are made.
A bank can be designated as limited-purpose if it's core business and product line is limited. Waterhouse is essentially a credit card bank.
Limited-purpose institutions are evaluated on the basis of their community development lending, qualified investments or community development services, the OCC said.
About 45 banks regulated by the OCC are designated as wholesale or limited-purpose institutions.
The OCC is scheduled to conduct a CRA evaluation of Waterhouse in September, an OCC spokesman said.

A consumer activist group has opposed the merger of Toronto-Dominion and Waterhouse Investor Services saying Waterhouse National Bank does not comply with the CRA. The company said it has a good record on CRA.
A Fed spokesman said the Fed would not comment on pending merger applications.
